name: Roman capital proportions
summary: Capital letters with the proportions of Roman stone inscriptions: some letters wide and round, some narrow, and each one built for the eye, not for one measure.
how: Draw O as a near circle, and M about as wide as the cap height.
Draw E, F, L and S at about half the width of O.
Set the stem at about one tenth of the cap height for a classical weight; for signs, increase it by up to half.
Cut serifs, or leave them out, but keep the width rules.

origin.note: The inscription at the base of Trajan's Column sets the model for Roman capitals.

adoptions.via: Nicolas Jenson prints in Venice with a roman face whose capitals follow Roman inscriptions.
Edward Johnston draws the London Underground block letters on the proportions of Roman capitals.
Hermann Zapf releases Optima, a sans serif whose shapes come from stone inscriptions he saw in Florence.

sources.title: Edward M. Catich, The Origin of the Serif (Catfish Press, 1968)
